content:
The Israelites had left Egypt, but Egypt had not completely left their hearts. They were walking through the wilderness toward the Promised Land, yet they still remembered the food, the pleasures, and the comforts of the very place from which Yahweh had delivered them. In the same way, the New Creation has been called out of this present world. We have begun our own wilderness journey along the narrow way. Christ said, "The gateway to life is very narrow and the road is difficult, and only a few ever find it" (Matthew 7:14). We are no longer walking according to the spirit of this world. We have left behind many customs, celebrations, habits, relationships, and desires that once controlled us. But during this journey, the greatest danger may not always come from an open enemy. Sometimes it comes through the people travelling near us.

In Numbers 11, the craving began with the foreign rabble, but it soon spread to the Israelites. The mixed multitude began speaking about Egypt's food, and before long the whole camp was weeping for the things they had left behind. In the same way, someone walking beside us may begin to say, "There is nothing wrong with this." Another may say, "You are being too strict." Someone else may say, "God will understand if you do it only once." They may tell us, "Attend this festival just this one time." They may say, "Go to this religious function; you do not have to participate fully." They may say, "Everyone in the family will be hurt if you refuse." They may say, "Just stand there for a few minutes; God knows your heart." They may say, "You have already left so many things; surely one small compromise will not matter." This is how the spirit of Egypt begins to speak to us again.

At first, it may sound harmless. It may even sound loving and reasonable. But slowly, it can create dissatisfaction in our heart. We may begin to feel that the narrow way is too strict. We may begin to remember the old celebrations, the old friendships, the old entertainment, the old traditions, and the old pleasures more fondly than the truth Yahweh has given us. And then, just like Israel, we may begin to murmur. We may say, "Why can others enjoy these things, but I cannot?" "Why must I always be different?" "Why does the way of truth require so much separation?" "Why can I not go back just for one day?" When these thoughts begin, we must remember that Israel's problem was not really about food at all. Their craving simply exposed a heart that was quietly turning away from Yahweh.

Proverbs 6:16-19 tells us there are six things Yahweh hates, and a seventh that is detestable to Him; proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that kill the innocent, a heart that plots evil, feet that race to do wrong, a false witness who pours out lies, and a person who sows discord among brothers and sisters. These same sins can quietly enter the New Creation during the wilderness journey. Proud eyes may cause us to think that Yahweh's directions do not need to apply to us; that we are strong enough to go anywhere and remain unaffected. A lying tongue may appear when we hide where we went, what we did, or why we attended a worldly or false religious function, telling one story to the brethren and another to our family. Hands that harm the innocent can appear when our compromise influences a weaker brother or sister, who sees us and thinks, "If they can do it, then so can I." A heart that plots evil begins when we secretly look for ways to satisfy our old desires while still appearing faithful before others. Feet that race toward wrong are seen when we quickly accept invitations that lead us back toward the spirit of Egypt. And a false witness appears when we call something harmless even though we know in our hearts it is against the direction Yahweh has given us.

But the seventh thing is the one who sows discord among the brethren, and this is exactly what the foreign rabble did. They did not keep their craving to themselves. Their words spread through the camp. Their dissatisfaction entered the hearts of others, and soon the whole congregation was crying.
The same thing can happen today. One person begins to question the truth. Another begins to defend compromise. A third person says, "We should not be so serious." And soon a whole group begins to drift away from the narrow way. This is why we must be very careful about whose voice we allow to guide us. Not everyone travelling near us is travelling with the same heart. Some may walk among the New Creation but still desire Egypt. Some may love the fellowship but not the separation. Some may enjoy the blessings of truth but still long for the celebrations and customs of the world. And their words can slowly weaken us. They may say, "Only this one time." But many spiritual falls begin with those very words. Only one celebration. Only one compromise.Only one false religious function. Only one secret visit. Only one worldly relationship. Only one step backward. But one step toward Egypt can become the beginning of a long journey away from Yahweh.

If we continue grumbling and demanding the things we left behind, Yahweh may sometimes allow us to have the very thing we insist upon.

Israel demanded meat, and God gave them meat; but the thing they desired became the very thing that destroyed them. Psalm 106:15 says, "So he gave them what they asked for, but he sent a plague along with it". This is a fearful lesson. Sometimes Yahweh's judgment is not that He takes something away from us. Sometimes the judgment is that He allows us to receive the very thing we demand. A person may insist on a certain relationship, and later that relationship becomes a spiritual trap. A person may fight for worldly success, and later that success takes away all their time for God. A person may refuse to separate from old customs, and later those customs pull the whole family away from truth. A person may demand the freedom to attend every celebration, and later that freedom becomes bondage. What we desire can become our noose. What we demand can become our grave. The Israelites thought the quail would satisfy them, but instead the meat became connected with their death.Their craving became their graves.

The same danger exists for the New Creation. If we keep looking back toward Egypt, the things we left behind may return with even greater power.

What once seemed like pleasure can become spiritual poison. What once seemed like freedom can destroy the New Creation life within us. James 1:14-15 says, "Temptation comes from our own desires. These desires give birth to sinful actions. And when sin is allowed to grow, it gives birth to death". Therefore we must learn how to remain on course. First, we must remember why God called us out. We did not leave the world because there was no pleasure in it. We left because its end is death. Second, we must remember the bondage behind the attraction. Israel remembered Egypt's fish but forgot Egypt's slavery. We must not remember only the enjoyment of our old life and forget the pain, the guilt, the darkness, and the separation from God that came with it.

Third, we must guard our ears. Not every friendly voice is a safe voice, and we must weigh every suggestion by the Word of God. Fourth, we must speak quickly when temptation begins. We should not hide our struggle until it grows strong; we should seek help from mature brethren and pray before the desire has time to take root. Fifth, we must keep our eyes on Christ. Hebrews 12:2 says, "We do this by keeping our eyes on Jesus, the champion who initiates and perfects our faith". The narrow way becomes dangerous when we look backward, but it becomes possible when we keep looking forward to Christ. And finally, we must learn to be satisfied with Yahweh's provision.
The Israelites despised the manna because they desired Egypt's variety, yet the manna was their very life in the wilderness. In the same way, prayer, Scripture, fellowship, obedience, and the daily guidance of Yahweh may appear simple, but these are the very things that preserve our spiritual life.

So let us be very careful when the people around us encourage us to move against God’s direction. Let us not allow another person's craving to become our craving. Let us not allow their complaint to become our complaint. Let us not allow their compromise to become our spiritual death. We have been called out of Egypt. We are walking through the wilderness. The Kingdom is before us. Let us remain on the narrow way, and never allow the pleasures we left behind to become the graves of the New Creation.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We thank You that You called us out of Egypt and set our faces toward Your Kingdom.

Guard our hearts so that Egypt does not creep back in through the voices around us.

Help us to remember not only the taste of the old life, but the chains that came with it.

Give us courage to say no to 'only this one time,' knowing where that road leads.

Teach us to be satisfied with Your daily provision, and never to despise it.

Keep our ears from unsafe voices and our eyes fixed forward upon Christ.

Let no one's craving become our craving, and no one's compromise become our grave.

"Turn my eyes from worthless things, and give me life through your word." - Psalm 119:37

In the name of Christ, the champion of our faith, we pray. Amen.
